userStories.title: Implement core RunTerminal component with ansi-to-html and incremental append
userStories.description: Replace src/components/RunTerminal.tsx with a new implementation using ansi-to-html. The component connects to GET /api/pipeline/runs/{runId}/output SSE, decodes base64 chunks, accumulates raw text in a useRef buffer, and flushes every 80ms via setTimeout. On each flush, convert ONLY the new buffered text using ansi-to-html and append the resulting HTML string to accumulated HTML state — never re-convert the full buffer. Render inside a <pre> tag with overflow-y: auto, white-space: pre-wrap, and a monospace font. On the done SSE event, flush immediately and close EventSource.
acceptanceCriteria: @xterm/xterm and @xterm/addon-fit are not imported anywhere in RunTerminal.tsx
SSE chunks are decoded from base64 and appended to a useRef text buffer — NOT converted immediately
An 80ms setTimeout timer is started on first pending chunk; when it fires, only new buffered text is converted via ansi-to-html and appended to HTML state
The pre element renders dangerouslySetInnerHTML with the accumulated HTML string
On the done SSE event, the buffer is flushed immediately (without waiting for the 80ms timer) and EventSource is closed
Late-joiner scenario: connecting to a run already in progress replays all prior chunks before live ones

RunTerminal exports a RunTerminalHandle type with scrollToStory(storyId) and writeMarker(text) methods via useImperativeHandle — RunViewPanel.tsx calls these via ref and must not break at compile time
scrollToStory(storyId) inserts anchor elements (e.g. data-story-id attributes) at story boundaries in the HTML output and uses scrollIntoView() to navigate to them
writeMarker(text) appends a visible styled marker line into the accumulated HTML output
Text selection and copy works natively via browser selection on the pre element — no programmatic buffer extraction (term.buffer.active.getLine) is needed since pre supports native Ctrl+C/Cmd+C

userStories.title: Implement scroll-lock awareness and 20,000-line buffer cap
userStories.description: Add scroll-lock detection to RunTerminal: track a scrollLocked boolean ref that is true when the user has scrolled up more than ~50px from the bottom. On each 80ms flush, only auto-scroll (scrollTop = scrollHeight) if scrollLocked is false. Add a scroll event listener to the pre container that updates scrollLocked. Implement a 20,000-line DOM cap: after appending new HTML, count total newlines in the accumulated HTML string; if exceeding 20,000, truncate the oldest lines by removing text up to and including the 20,000th-oldest newline boundary. No react-window or virtualization.
acceptanceCriteria: Auto-scroll fires after each flush only when user is within ~50px of the bottom of the pre container
When user scrolls up past the 50px threshold, auto-scroll stops — subsequent new chunks do not reposition the viewport
When user scrolls back to the bottom, auto-scroll resumes on the next flush
The accumulated HTML string is capped at 20,000 lines: oldest content is trimmed when exceeded
Trimming does not break mid-ANSI-tag HTML (truncation occurs at a newline boundary)
No virtualization library (react-window, react-virtual, etc.) is introduced

=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
principles:
  typescript:
    strict_mode: true
    target: ES2022
    no_any: "Avoid `any` — use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generics"
    async_first: "All DB calls, LLM calls, and I/O are async — always await"

  error_handling:
    pattern: "AppError class hierarchy with immutable HTTP status codes"
    subclasses: [ValidationError 400, AuthError 401, ForbiddenError 403, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, UnprocessableError 422]
    serialization: "{ error: string, code?: string, details?: Record<string, unknown> }"
    rule: "Throw from route handlers; centralized errorHandler middleware catches and serializes"

  database:
    driver: "pg Pool (async, connection pooling)"
    helpers: "query<T>() returns T[], queryOne<T>() returns T|undefined, execute() returns { rowCount }"
    placeholders: "$1, $2, ... (numbered, NOT positional ?)"
    transactions: "transaction<T>(fn) wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK"
    migrations: "SQL files in pg-migrations/, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files, tracked in schema_migrations"
    slow_query_logging: "Queries > 500ms logged with sanitized params"

  validation:
    library: zod
    pattern: "Middleware factories — validateBody(schema), validateQuery(schema), validateParams(schema)"
    method: "safeParse (not .parse() which throws)"
    response: "{ error: firstIssueMessage, details: zodError.issues }"

  llm:
    return_type: "ChatResult { text: string, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens } }"
    rule: "Always use .text accessor — never treat ChatResult as a string"
    providers: "Multi-provider routing via model registry — claude-cli, anthropic, openai-compat, openrouter"

  api_design:
    documentation: "JSDoc @swagger annotations on every route → auto-generated OpenAPI spec"
    pagination: "{ items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }"
    response_shape: "Success: res.json(data). Error: { error, code, details } via AppError"
    middleware_chain: "validateBody(schema) → authRequired → async handler"
    security_headers: "helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, noSniff, referrerPolicy)"
    caching: "Cache-Control: no-store on all responses, etag: false"

  testing:
    backend: "Jest with ts-jest, serial (maxWorkers: 1), 30s timeout, PG_POOL_SIZE=1"
    frontend: "Vitest with jsdom, globals: true"
    rule: "Always clean up DB pool connections in afterAll()"

  code_style:
    no_over_engineering: "Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly necessary"
    no_premature_abstraction: "Three similar lines > premature helper function"
    minimal_containers: "Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't change"
    security_first: "Never commit .env files, API keys, or secrets. Use vault for sensitive values."

=== PROJECT CONTEXT (L3) ===

  - backend/src/lib/ — core services (sse-hub, direction-stack, llm-client, execution-engine, context-router, workspace-echolocation, rate-limiter, scheduler)

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Terminal & SSE Architecture Overhaul: Replace the xterm.js terminal renderer and WAL polling system with a lightweight, production-ready architecture. Three changes, no new frameworks, no rewrites.

STORY 1 + 3: Replace xterm.js with ansi-to-html + <pre> in RunTerminal
Remove @xterm/xterm and @xterm/addon-fit dependencies entirely. Replace RunTerminal.tsx with a component that uses the ansi-to-html library to convert ANSI escape codes to HTML, rendered inside a <pre> tag with overflow-y: auto. Connect to the same GET /api/pipeline/runs/{runId}/output SSE endpoint and decode base64 chunks identically.

Critical constraints:
- Incremental HTML append: each 80ms flush ONLY converts NEW chunks to HTML and appends to accumulated HTML string in state — do NOT re-convert entire buffer on every flush (catastrophic CPU on 50k+ line builds)
- 80ms batch flush: accumulate raw decoded text in a useRef buffer; on each SSE chunk append to ref; if no flush timer pending start 80ms setTimeout; when timer fires convert ONLY new buffered text via ansi-to-html, append to HTML state, clear ref buffer, conditionally auto-scroll
- Scroll-lock awareness: only auto-scroll if user is within ~50px of bottom; if scrolled up reading history, do NOT yank them down every 80ms
- Buffer cap at 20,000 lines: truncate oldest lines from DOM if exceeded — no react-window, no virtualization
- Theme support: preserve dark/light theme switching via ThemeContext, map xterm color palette to ansi-to-html foreground/background options
- Late-joiner replay: full history replay on connect, then live chunks
- On done event: flush immediately (don't wait for 80ms timer) and close EventSource
- Remove @xterm/xterm, @xterm/addon-fit, and xterm.css from package.json and all imports

STORY 2: Replace WAL polling with Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY
Remove the 1-second polling interval in /api/pipeline/stream SSE endpoint in backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts. Replace with Postgres LISTEN subscription.

Implementation:
- Create Postgres trigger function notify_wal_event() that calls pg_notify('wal_events', row_to_json(NEW)::text) after each INSERT on wal_events table; create corresponding AFTER INSERT trigger
- In backend, establish dedicated long-lived Postgres client connection (separate from query pool) that runs LISTEN wal_events; on each notification parse JSON payload and broadcast via existing sse-hub.ts broadcastAll()
- Handle reconnection: if LISTEN connection drops, reconnect with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, max 30s)
- Trigger and function created via new timestamp-format migration file in backend/src/db/pg-migrations/
- Delete polling interval code and lastSeenId tracking
- usePipelineSSE hook on frontend requires ZERO changes

Out of scope: No Web Workers, no SharedWorkers, no virtualization libraries, no framework changes, no canvas renderers. The backend SSE output endpoint (/api/pipeline/runs/{runId}/output) requires zero changes — only the consumer changes. Story 2 is fully independent and can run in parallel with Story 1.
